sources.quote: testimonials or endorsements however communicated, any person, character or animal, and lifestyle promotion evoking glamour, recreation, excitement, vitality, risk or daring
sources.title: Cannabis Act ( SC 2018, c. 16) - Justice Laws Website
sources.evidence: Section 17(1): unless authorized under the Act, it is prohibited to promote cannabis or a cannabis accessory or any service related to cannabis by means of a testimonial or endorsement, however displayed or communicated; by means of the depiction of a person, character or animal, whether real or fictional; or by presenting it in a manner that associates it with a way of life such as one that includes glamour, recreation, excitement, vitality, risk or daring.

sources.quote: the federal promotion exception for telecommunication applies only where reasonable steps keep a young person from the material
sources.title: Promotion of cannabis: Prohibitions and permissions in the Cannabis Act and Regulations - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Cannabis can be promoted by means of a telecommunication where the person responsible for the content of the promotion has taken reasonable steps to ensure that the promotion cannot be accessed by a young person. Steps that may be easily circumvented by youth may require additional steps.

sources.quote: 19 in most provinces, 18 in Alberta, 21 in Quebec
sources.title: Authorized cannabis retailers in the provinces and territories - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Alberta has a legal age of 18, while Quebec has a legal age of 21. Most other provinces and territories set the minimum age at 19.

sources.quote: Ontario made curbside pick-up and delivery permanent in March 2022, with delivery by the authorization holder or their own staff rather than a courier, inside set hours
sources.publisher: Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
sources.title: Information Bulletin - Supporting Cannabis Retailers: Curbside Pick-up and Delivery to Become Permanent on March 15 | Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
sources.evidence: The Government of Ontario established new rules to enable cannabis retailers to offer delivery and curbside pick-up services on a permanent basis beginning March 15, 2022. Delivery can only be done by the RSA holder or their employees, and third party delivery is not permitted. Cannabis may only be delivered between 9 a.m. and 11 p.m.

sources.quote: a retailer's website or app must take reasonable measures to confirm the customer is at least 19, and must display the official Ontario cannabis retail seal with the applicable store authorization information
sources.publisher: Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
sources.title: Operating a Store | Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
sources.evidence: Licensees must take reasonable measures to ensure that individuals accessing their website, app or other similar online platform for the purpose of the cannabis retail store are at least 19 years of age. Licensees must display the official Ontario cannabis retail seal and make available the applicable CRSA information (the authorization number, the holder's name, the store's operating name and the store address) on websites, apps or other similar online platforms.

sources.quote: It did open a limited Canadian pilot in 2025 allowing some cannabis ads on Search only
sources.title: Update to cannabis-related content policy (January 2026) - Advertising Policies Help
sources.evidence: Google Ads is launching a limited pilot programme in Canada for specific, legally allowed cannabis-related product types or services. This pilot will run on Search only, beginning on 25 August 2025, through 31 December 2026.

sources.quote: The Cannabis Regulation Act makes the SQDC the province's only lawful retailer, sets the minimum age at 21 and bans promotional gifts, rebates, contests and sponsorship
sources.title: The legislation on cannabis in brief | Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: Only the Société québécoise du cannabis (SQDC) is authorized for the retail sale of cannabis in Québec. A person under 21 years of age may not be admitted to a cannabis retail outlet. It is prohibited to give or supply cannabis for promotional purposes, to offer consumers a gift or rebate or a right to participate in a lottery, contest or game, or to give consumers a rebate on the market price.

flags.quote: Ontario caps any single operator at 75 store authorizations
flags.issue: Outdated. The AGCO retail store authorization page states that an applicant, together with its affiliates, cannot hold more than 150 cannabis retail store authorizations; the 75-store cap was the earlier limit.
